chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the marriage of the Jewish woman and the Christian woman, so he said, 'There is no harm in it. Do you not know that a Jewish woman was under the marriage of Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah during the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)?'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is marriage to a Jewish or Christian woman permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the permissibility of marrying Jewish and Christian women, grounding this ruling in the established precedent of Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah’s marriage to a Jewish woman during the Prophet’s era. This narration, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlights the continuity of early Islamic practice and serves as a primary evidentiary basis for the Shia jurisprudential view on *Kitabiyyat* (People of the Book).
